title: Finite-block arithmetic cochain Roos comparison
statement: Let $A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with countable products [def-weil-category-product] and inverse limits of towers. Use the arithmetic restriction $r_e$, termwise limit $L$, limit restriction $\alpha_e$, boundary $\delta$, selection $a_e$, block map $b_e$, and actual mapping cocone $M$ from [def-sp-strict-tower-arithmetic-restriction-data]. For $e\geq1$ and a cochain complex $I$ of towers such that each tower $I^i$ is injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions], the strict square $\delta_I b_e=a_e\delta_{r_eI}$ holds. There exist quasi-isomorphisms $\kappa:LI\to M(I)$, $\kappa_e:Lr_eI\to M(r_eI)$, and $c:M(I)\to M(r_eI)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. In every cochain degree, composing the first coordinate of $\kappa$ with product projection $n$ is the ordinary limit projection at $n$; the analogous coordinate of $\kappa_e$ is the restricted limit projection. Both second coordinates vanish. The first coordinate of $c$ is the first coordinate of $M(I)$ followed by $a_e$, and its second coordinate in degree $i$ is the second coordinate of $M(I)$ followed by $b_e$ in degree $i-1$. Finally $\kappa c=\alpha_e\kappa_e$.

proof.text: Embed an injective tower J into its functorial finite-product split envelope E(J). The pointwise monic embedding is a tower mono, so injectivity retracts it. Compose the embedding at n, a section of the envelope transition, and the retraction at n+1 to split the original transition. Compose sections for arbitrary blocks. The recursion x_0=0, x_(n+1)=sigma_n(x_n-y_n) splits one minus shift degreewise; evaluation preserves the chosen products, transporting this splitting to the evaluated complex boundary.

Its two coordinates prove the kernel square, and two-out-of-three with the initial-index ordinary-limit isomorphism proves it is a quasi-isomorphism.

theorem strictTowerArithmeticRestrictionCochainModel
    (A : Type a) [Category.{b} A] [Abelian A]
    [HasCountableProducts A] [HasLimitsOfShape ℕᵒᵖ A]
    (e : ℕ) (he : 1 ≤ e) (I : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ℤ)
    (hI : ∀ i : ℤ, Injective (I.X i)) :
        boundary I ≫ block e I.asFunctor =
          selection e I.asFunctor ≫ boundary ((complexRestriction _ e).obj I) ∧
        ∃ (κ : (limitComplex _).obj I ⟶ model I)
          (κe : (limitComplex _).obj ((complexRestriction _ e).obj I) ⟶
            model ((complexRestriction _ e).obj I))
          (c : model I ⟶ model ((complexRestriction _ e).obj I)),
          QuasiIso κ ∧ QuasiIso κe ∧ QuasiIso c ∧
          (∀ (i : ℤ) (n : ℕ),
            κ.f i ≫ (CochainComplex.mappingCocone.fst (boundary I)).f i ≫
                (Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ I.asFunctor.obj (op n)) n).f i =
              limit.π (I.X i) (op n)) ∧
          (∀ (i j : ℤ) (h : i + -1 = j),
            κ.f i ≫ (CochainComplex.mappingCocone.snd (boundary I)).v i j h = 0) ∧
          (∀ (i : ℤ) (n : ℕ),
            κe.f i ≫ (CochainComplex.mappingCocone.fst
                (boundary ((complexRestriction _ e).obj I))).f i ≫
                (Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ I.asFunctor.obj ((index e).obj (op n))) n).f i =
              limit.π (((complexRestriction _ e).obj I).X i) (op n)) ∧
          (∀ (i j : ℤ) (h : i + -1 = j),
            κe.f i ≫ (CochainComplex.mappingCocone.snd
              (boundary ((complexRestriction _ e).obj I))).v i j h = 0) ∧
          c ≫ CochainComplex.mappingCocone.fst (boundary ((complexRestriction _ e).obj I)) =
            CochainComplex.mappingCocone.fst (boundary I) ≫ selection e I.asFunctor ∧
          (∀ (i j : ℤ) (h : i + -1 = j),
            c.f i ≫ (CochainComplex.mappingCocone.snd
                (boundary ((complexRestriction _ e).obj I))).v i j h =
              (CochainComplex.mappingCocone.snd (boundary I)).v i j h ≫
                (block e I.asFunctor).f j) ∧
          κ ≫ c = limitMap e I ≫ κe
